guide.mmcr_patchouli.entry.basics.overvi: A modular machine usually consists of a controller, structural blocks, and functional components.$(br2)The controller checks structure and manages operation. Input ports supply recipe inputs, such as materials and energy; output ports collect products. Casings form the machine's structure.$(br2)Start with the $(l:mmcr:controllers/controller)controller$(/l), then choose components to match the machine's requirements.

Machines come from modpacks or addons. Without custom machine content, no machine controllers will be available, but this guide remains readable.$(br2)Parallel controllers, factory controllers, upgrade buses, and advanced modules only serve a purpose when supported by the machine. Placing them in a structure does not mean the machine recognizes them.
guide.mmcr_patchouli.entry.basics.acquis: Craft an ordinary book with a Modularium Ingot in a shapeless recipe to obtain the Modular Machinery Guide. Ingredient positions do not matter.
Modularium Ingots are this mod's basic crafting material, unless the recipes have been customized.
With Patchouli installed, you can also find the guide in the MMCR creative tab. Without Patchouli, neither the book nor its recipe is provided.
guide.mmcr_patchouli.entry.basics.casing: The basic casing is a decorative block provided by MMCR. Apart from being a basic crafting material for ports, it has no special function.
guide.mmcr_patchouli.entry.controllers.c: The machine controller is the core block of a machine. Each machine's controller is registered dynamically with its machine content.

Facing orients the structure. Vertical placement needs machine support; facing depends on the clicked face and player position.$(br2)Place the controller first, then check with a $(l:mmcr:tools/blueprint)blueprint$(/l) or $(l:mmcr:tools/terminal)terminal$(/l). Horizontal-only machines cannot face vertically.

$(l:mmcr:processing/factory)Factory controllers$(/l) schedule supported machines; they do not replace machine controllers.$(br2)The machine's own controller still checks structure and runs recipes. It shows factory threads when enabled. The factory component's screen holds thread-capacity items.
guide.mmcr_patchouli.entry.controllers.f: Right-click the controller to open the machine screen.$(br2)For an unformed machine, empty both hands and sneak-right-click the controller. This sends a structure preview and requests an immediate check.$(br2)You can also use the $(l:mmcr:tools/terminal)terminal's Check function$(/l).

Use the preview to check block types, states, positions, and counts. Port direction (input or output), family, and tier also affect formation requirements; a larger port is not necessarily a valid substitute.$(br2)For multi-stage structures, select the correct structure stage.

Shared components must follow the machine's sharing restrictions. Overlapping structures do not mean every port can serve both machines.$(br2)It is best to keep the structure area loaded; doing so causes no performance loss.
guide.mmcr_patchouli.entry.controllers.o: Formed does not mean running.$(br2)Read status, recipe, and progress. Idle, no recipe, insufficient resources, and paused are different states. During operation, product and energy information reflects the current recipe and actual parallelism.

Machines only select recipes from their available recipe pools.$(br2)Machine level and structure stage are different: the former comes from conditions such as level slots, while the latter describes a phase of the whole structure. Recipes may require both.

A direct redstone signal pauses the controller.$(br2)Follow the screen's failure reason to check inputs, energy, output space, and extra conditions. Do not judge operation by appearance alone. See $(l:mmcr:troubleshooting/common)troubleshooting$(/l).
guide.mmcr_patchouli.entry.ports.items.p: Input buses hold items for recipes to consume. Right-click to open the screen and insert materials, or supply them by other means, such as pipes. The machine must recognize the bus as a valid input component.
Output buses receive machine products. Leave compatible space available for those items.

Normal bus tiers differ in slot layout. $(l:mmcr:ports/extended_items)Extended item buses$(/l) store bulk items and display actual amounts. Larger storage does not relax structure rules.$(br2)For automatic supply or product removal, choose resource type and faces on the $(l:mmcr:ports/auto_io)auto-IO page$(/l).
Fluid input hatches supply fluids to machines. Right-click with a supported fluid container to interact according to port direction and container capabilities. You can also connect fluid transport equipment, such as pipes.
Fluid output hatches receive fluid products for removal by containers or transport equipment. Incompatible contents or insufficient free space can block output.

For bulk fluid storage, see $(l:mmcr:ports/extended_fluids)extended fluid hatches$(/l).$(br2)Insufficient input and insufficient output space are separate problems. Chemicals cannot be stored here as ordinary fluids.
Energy input hatches store energy consumed by machines. Connect a working supply and check the required input tier. Insufficient stored energy can interrupt recipe operation.
Energy output hatches receive energy generated by recipes and transfer it outside the machine.

$(l:mmcr:ports/extended_energy)Extended energy hatches$(/l) offer greater capacity and transfer rates.$(br2)For unstable operation, check stored energy, the power source, and $(l:mmcr:ports/auto_io)auto IO$(/l).
guide.mmcr_patchouli.entry.ports.combine: A combined input port provides item and fluid inputs in one block. Each resource has separate storage and auto-IO settings.
A combined output port receives both item and fluid products. Both sides need free space; blockage on either side can affect the entire recipe.

$(l:mmcr:ports/extended_combined)Extended combined ports$(/l) provide bulk item and fluid storage. Structure and port requirements together determine whether they can replace separate buses or hatches.$(br2)Configure items and fluids separately on the $(l:mmcr:ports/auto_io)auto-IO page$(/l).
guide.mmcr_patchouli.entry.ports.auto_io: Right-click a port that supports auto IO, then use the page-switch button to open its controls. Multi-resource ports let you select items, fluids, and other resource types separately.$(br2)Input ports pull from adjacent storage; output ports push to adjacent receivers. Master and side switches apply to the selected resource type.

Click the six face buttons to toggle automatic transfer for each face. The buttons can show adjacent blocks.$(br2)Turning off the master switch stops automatic transfer even on enabled faces. Neighbors must support the resource and allow extraction or insertion in the required direction.

Eject Contents on an input port tries to return the selected resource to adjacent receivers. Click for the first resource kind; Shift-click to request all kinds.$(br2)Ports used by active recipes cannot eject. Without a receiver, contents stay inside. Output ports do not have this button.
guide.mmcr_patchouli.entry.processing.pa: Parallel controllers raise the batch-processing limit for a supported machine. Tiers have different limits; the effective result still depends on machine and recipe settings.

Parallelism batches copies of one recipe; it does not add independent threads.$(br2)Actual batches depend on materials, output space, energy, and machine conditions, not just the limit. Check $(l:mmcr:ports/items)items$(/l), $(l:mmcr:ports/fluids)fluids$(/l), and $(l:mmcr:ports/energy)energy$(/l).
guide.mmcr_patchouli.entry.processing.fa: Factory controllers schedule multiple recipe threads for factory-capable machines. Put this component in a permitted structure position. It is not a complete machine on its own.

The machine controller's factory screen shows each thread's status and progress. Factory threads run recipes independently; $(l:mmcr:processing/parallel)parallelism$(/l) batches work within one thread.$(br2)$(l:mmcr:processing/thread_disperser)Thread Rippers$(/l) add scheduling capacity. Machine limits, recipe thread caps, and shared input/output resources still limit actual operation.
guide.mmcr_patchouli.entry.processing.th: Place Thread Rippers in the factory controller's dedicated item slot.

Slot contents contribute to thread capacity; changes update the linked factory.$(br2)This is not a CPU setting or a guarantee of one running recipe per item. Check $(l:mmcr:processing/factory)factory support$(/l), resources, and recipe thread limits first.
guide.mmcr_patchouli.entry.components.up: Upgrade buses hold upgrade items supported by the machine. Bus families offer different slot counts.

Insert the upgrades specified by the machine's instructions. They may affect operating conditions or processing capabilities; types and stacking rules depend on the machine and upgrade definitions.$(br2)If they have no effect, check structure recognition and item support first. Ordinary materials and thread-capacity items are not universal upgrades.
guide.mmcr_patchouli.entry.components.sm: Smart interfaces provide editable numeric parameters for a linked machine. Available types come from that machine. Without a valid binding or defined parameters, there is nothing to edit.

Right-click to open the screen, select a parameter, and read its description and current value. Enter a number, then click Save or press Enter; integer parameters do not accept fractions.$(br2)Values may affect recipe conditions or machine effects, as defined by the machine. Saving a value does not guarantee it satisfies the target recipe.
guide.mmcr_patchouli.entry.components.da: Data storage holds a linked machine's runtime data and provides no ordinary item input/output. Use it only when needed by the machine's structure and behavior.
Data storage links to at most one controller. The machine can save and read its data. Whether it appears in the machine screen and how it affects operation depend on the machine.
guide.mmcr_patchouli.entry.components.mo: A module bridge connects a supported host and module. Both structures must use the same bridge at valid positions, and the host must allow that module type.

Check that both the host and module are formed, then check their connection. A formed but offline module may still be unable to run.$(br2)The bridge must uniquely link a valid host and module. Overlapping shared functional interfaces can cause conflicts. If connection fails, check allowed types, structures, and bridge positions; placing a module beside a host is not enough.
guide.mmcr_patchouli.entry.tools.bluepri: Sneak-right-click a machine controller while holding a blueprint to bind its machine. Then hold the blueprint in your main hand and right-click the air to open the structure preview.

Plus/minus buttons select display layers; A shows all layers and R resets the view. Multi-stage machines also have previous/next stage buttons.$(br2)A layer is a viewing slice along the Y axis; a structure stage is a phase of the whole structure. Click preview blocks for allowed replacements. The material list reflects the current preview.

The tooltip's material list uses the lowest structure stage and default-level blocks; hold Shift to expand it.$(br2)When building, check the screen's structure stage and replacement options. Use a $(l:mmcr:tools/terminal)terminal$(/l) to select a specific building level. Blueprints do not place blocks automatically.
guide.mmcr_patchouli.entry.tools.termina: Main-hand sneak-right-click binds a controller. Air right-click opens the screen; sneak-use in air unbinds the controller and resets structure selections and preview. Stay within operating distance.

Inventory mode uses your materials. Select container mode in the screen, then sneak-right-click a valid container to bind it. Clear keeps the inventory mode, container binding, and wireless access point binding.$(br2)Choose the structure stage and machine level, then use Preview, display layers, and Check to verify the target. Checking is not building. See $(l:mmcr:controllers/formation)formation checks$(/l).

Build takes materials from the selected inventory and places blocks allowed by the machine.$(br2)Demolish targets the selected structure and returns recoverable items to the selected inventory. Leave room for returns; it is not a tool for mining arbitrary regions.

Keep the terminal in your main hand during operation. The controller must be in the same dimension and within the server-configured operating radius; target chunks must also be loaded.$(br2)Unavailable containers or other inventories prevent building and demolition. Preview only shows the target, not whether structure or inventory requirements are met. Follow the binding, distance, and material status messages.
guide.mmcr_patchouli.entry.tools.export_: A developer tool available only in creative mode.$(br2)The multiblock export tool marks regions for structure creation and export. Right-click a block for the first corner; sneak-right-click for the second. While holding the tool, use Pick Block to mark the controller position and face.

Hold the tool in your main hand and right-click the air to open settings; sneak-use in the air to clear the selection. The tooltip lists recorded positions.$(br2)Inspect existing machines with a $(l:mmcr:tools/blueprint)blueprint$(/l) and build with a $(l:mmcr:tools/terminal)terminal$(/l).
guide.mmcr_patchouli.entry.network.inter: A network interface is a machine-network endpoint that must be recognized by a valid formed machine. It is not an AE2 ME interface, and connecting a cable does not make it an ME storage port.

Connections need machine support, allowed endpoint types, free connection capacity, and valid machine states.$(br2)Use a $(l:mmcr:network/key_card)key card$(/l) to select source and target. Adding an interface does not give every machine new network features.
guide.mmcr_patchouli.entry.network.key_c: Sneak-right-click a valid network interface to select the source endpoint. Normally right-click the target interface to attempt a connection. Sneak-use in the air to clear the card's selection.

The selected source interface must belong to a valid formed machine. An invalid source machine or interface, invalid target, disallowed type, or full connection capacity rejects the connection with a message.$(br2)If it fails, check the $(l:mmcr:network/interfaces)network interface conditions$(/l) and reselect the source if needed.
guide.mmcr_patchouli.entry.troubleshooti: $(bold)Structure first$(reset)$(br)Check facing, blocks, port tiers, stage, and loaded chunks with $(l:mmcr:controllers/formation)formation checks$(/l).$(br2)Then verify the recipe pool, machine level, and structure stage support the target recipe.

$(bold)Resources next$(reset)$(br)Put materials in $(l:mmcr:ports/items)input buses$(/l) or the correct fluid inputs. Maintain enough $(l:mmcr:ports/energy)energy$(/l) and compatible output space.$(br2)Check $(l:mmcr:ports/auto_io)auto IO$(/l): resource type, master switch, faces, and adjacent storage. Higher parallelism needs more materials and output space.

$(bold)Extra conditions$(reset)$(br)Remove pausing redstone signals. Check $(l:mmcr:components/modules)module connections$(/l) and $(l:mmcr:components/smart_interface)parameters$(/l).$(br2)Capacity is not active threads; an offline network is not a missing structure. Follow the controller's status and failure reason.
Connect to an ME network and configure items or fluids to stock in the interface screen. Normal input interfaces first stock their own storage; the machine consumes this local inventory.

Meet machine structure rules and ME network conditions. Check actual interface contents, not just stocking targets.$(br2)A configured target is not owned material. For direct network-stock consumption, see $(l:mmcr:ae2/me_stocking_input)stocking inputs$(/l).
guide.mmcr_patchouli.entry.ae2.me_stocki: Configure the item or fluid types the machine may use. Stocking inputs consume ME network inventory directly. Displayed storage amounts mirror network stock, not a separate local cache already collected in the block.

Unlike $(l:mmcr:ae2/me_input)normal inputs$(/l), no local stock accumulates. Recipes extract configured types from ME; settings do not create inventory.$(br2)Keep the network usable and stocked. Disconnection or other consumers change displayed and available amounts.
guide.mmcr_patchouli.entry.ae2.me_output: Send machine items and fluids into the ME network. Normal output interfaces have a bounded local cache; network scheduling continues moving cached products into storage.

An offline network, missing compatible storage, or insufficient space prevents the cache from draining. A full cache then blocks machine output.$(br2)Check network power, connectivity, and storage space. $(l:mmcr:ae2/me_async_output)Async outputs$(/l) buffer differently.
guide.mmcr_patchouli.entry.ae2.me_async_: Async outputs receive products in a temporary in-memory queue, then send batches through ME network scheduling. They do not use the normal output's persisted local cache and have no offline-storage fallback.

Unloading, removal, or inactive nodes clear undelivered contents. Keep network and chunks available.$(br2)Async means neither unlimited capacity nor guaranteed speed. Acceptance needs network insertion space. For local caching, use $(l:mmcr:ae2/me_output)normal outputs$(/l).
guide.mmcr_patchouli.entry.ae2.me_patter: Insert processing patterns matching machine recipes and connect the interface to ME. It coordinates AE2 crafting requests with linked machines; it cannot make a machine execute a recipe it does not have.

Starts require formed, runnable machines, matching recipes, resources, idle threads, and batch/thread limits.$(br2)Products enter the provider's return inventory. AE2 returns them to ME to settle crafting. If ME cannot accept them, resolve return blockage.

Pattern and blocking settings govern request continuation, not exemptions from structure, redstone, or resource rules.$(br2)Distinguish $(l:mmcr:processing/factory)factory threads$(/l) from $(l:mmcr:processing/parallel)batch parallelism$(/l). For stalls, inspect machine status and AE2 return inventory.
guide.mmcr_patchouli.entry.ae2.terminal_: Choose ME inventory mode in the terminal, then hold it in your main hand and sneak-right-click a valid AE2 wireless access point. Bind the machine controller separately. An ordinary container is not a wireless access point.

Use a loaded, active access point with network inventory. Build extracts materials; demolition returns items.$(br2)Controller dimension and distance limits still apply. Follow shortages, network failures, and return failures. See $(l:mmcr:tools/terminal)terminal basics$(/l).
guide.mmcr_patchouli.entry.extendedae.in: Extended inputs offer more configuration and storage slots, still stocking locally before machine consumption. Direction matches $(l:mmcr:ae2/me_input)normal inputs$(/l).

Extended stocking inputs configure more resource types while retaining $(l:mmcr:ae2/me_stocking_input)direct network consumption$(/l). More slots do not turn the displayed network-stock mirror into a local cache.
Extended outputs offer a larger slot layout and send products to ME through a bounded local cache. See $(l:mmcr:ae2/me_output)normal output blockage conditions$(/l).

Oversize inputs use an oversize interface storage layout and still stock locally. Check configuration and amounts in the screen. Whether the port can replace another structure block remains the machine's decision.
Oversize outputs use the oversize interface storage layout to send machine products into ME. Insufficient network space still blocks output.

Extended pattern interfaces provide more pattern slots while retaining $(l:mmcr:ae2/me_pattern)pattern requests and product returns$(/l). More pattern slots do not increase actual machine threads or remove resource limits.

For stocking inputs, extended stocking interfaces are sufficient.$(br2)Input, stocking, output, and pattern interfaces serve different tasks. Do not choose or interchange them just because a name sounds larger.
guide.mmcr_patchouli.entry.appflux.flux_: ME flux input interfaces supply machines from AppliedFlux's ME energy storage. They need a working network, extractable energy, and machine support for this input component.

ME flux output interfaces send generated energy into AppliedFlux network storage. Insufficient acceptance space affects output. Input and output are not interchangeable; see $(l:mmcr:ports/energy)energy direction and supply$(/l).
guide.mmcr_patchouli.entry.mekanism.chem: Chemical input hatches supply Mekanism chemicals. Chemicals differ from ordinary fluids; fluid input hatches are not substitutes. Normal chemical hatches accept only non-radioactive chemicals.
Chemical output hatches receive non-radioactive chemical products for removal by chemical transport equipment. Check product type, direction, and free space first.

Hatch tiers differ in storage and may satisfy port-tier requirements. Larger capacity does not guarantee structure acceptance.$(br2)Check chemical type, amount, and $(l:mmcr:ports/auto_io)auto IO$(/l). Radioactive materials need $(l:mmcr:mekanism/radioactivity)radioactive hatches$(/l).
guide.mmcr_patchouli.entry.mekanism.radi: Radioactive inputs accept only chemicals with the radioactive property, for machine consumption. Normal chemical hatches reject these resources; radioactive hatches also reject ordinary non-radioactive chemicals.

Radioactive outputs receive radioactive chemical products. Extract them with a receiver supporting the resource, and confirm machine support for this port. It does not convert products into non-radioactive chemicals.

Radioactive hatches are storage ports restricted by chemical type. They do not purify, remove radiation, or process waste.$(br2)Removal invokes radiation dumping for their contents when Mekanism radiation is enabled. Handle contents through valid transport before dismantling. Storage support does not mean radiation-free removal.
guide.mmcr_patchouli.entry.mekanism.heat: Heat inputs accept incoming external heat to satisfy machine heat or minimum-temperature conditions. Reaching a temperature threshold is not the same as storing enough heat. Check the actual recipe condition.

Heat outputs receive generated heat and transfer it to supported adjacent equipment. Output ports do not accept external heat coming in. Effective heat removal also depends on temperature difference and neighboring equipment.

Heat is stored energy; temperature describes thermal state; heat capacity determines temperature changes for a given amount of heat. They are not interchangeable capacity values.$(br2)Heat hatches lose heat to cooler surroundings, so temperature may drop when heating stops. Check heat and temperature readings, connected faces, and recipe conditions.
guide.mmcr_patchouli.entry.ports.extende: Extended Item Buses
Basic Input
The Basic extended input bus has 8 bulk storage positions for recipe materials. Each position holds an item type with its components. Use it for large reserves of the same materials.
Basic Output
The Basic extended item output bus has 8 bulk storage positions for machine products.
Advanced Input
The Advanced extended item input bus has 16 bulk storage positions. Choose this tier when a recipe pool needs more material types.
Advanced Output
The Advanced extended item output bus has 16 bulk storage positions to buffer more product types.
Reinforced In
The Reinforced extended item input bus has 24 bulk storage positions. It suits machines with many material types.
Reinforced Out
The Reinforced extended item output bus has 24 bulk storage positions to keep more product types separate.
Ultimate Input
The Ultimate extended item input bus has 32 bulk storage positions, the largest layout in this family.
Ultimate Output
The Ultimate extended item output bus has 32 bulk storage positions. It is suited to large product buffers.

All four tiers use large-quantity storage per position; upgrading increases the number of positions. Read actual amounts in the interface rather than treating them as ordinary stack sizes.$(br2)Use $(l:mmcr:ports/auto_io)auto IO$(/l) for supply or removal. Structure rules decide whether an extended bus can replace a normal one.
Extended Fluid Hatches
Basic Input
The Basic extended fluid input hatch has 8 bulk fluid storage positions. Supply the fluids required by the recipe through supported containers or neighboring fluid transport equipment.
Basic Output
The Basic extended fluid output hatch has 8 bulk fluid storage positions for fluid products.
Advanced Input
The Advanced extended fluid input hatch has 16 bulk fluid storage positions for a wider selection of recipe fluids.
Advanced Output
The Advanced extended fluid output hatch has 16 bulk fluid storage positions.
Reinforced In
The Reinforced extended fluid input hatch has 24 bulk fluid storage positions. It suits machines that use many fluid types.
Reinforced Out
The Reinforced extended fluid output hatch has 24 bulk fluid storage positions.
Ultimate Input
The Ultimate extended fluid input hatch has 32 bulk fluid storage positions, the largest layout in this family.
Ultimate Output
The Ultimate extended fluid output hatch has 32 bulk fluid storage positions for large amounts of varied fluid products.

The four tiers provide 8, 16, 24, or 32 fluid positions with large-quantity storage. Check actual amounts and fluid identities in the interface.$(br2)Configure $(l:mmcr:ports/auto_io)auto-IO faces$(/l) to match neighboring equipment. Structure rules still decide which hatch and direction are accepted.
Extended Energy Hatches
Reinforced In
The Reinforced extended energy input hatch buffers energy for power-consuming recipes.
Reinforced Out
The Reinforced extended energy output hatch receives energy from generating recipes.
Ultimate Input
The Ultimate extended energy input hatch offers greater capacity and a higher transfer limit than Reinforced. It suits high-energy recipes.
Ultimate Output
The Ultimate extended energy output hatch offers a larger buffer for generated energy and a higher transfer limit.

This family has Reinforced and Ultimate tiers, each with input and output versions. Their transfer rates reach the maximum available in gameplay.$(br2)Check $(l:mmcr:ports/auto_io)auto IO$(/l), adjacent energy capabilities, and the source or receiver. An output hatch does not replace the input needed by a power-consuming recipe.
Extended Combined Ports
Advanced Input
The Advanced extended combined input port supplies items and fluids from one block. It has 6 item positions and 2 fluid positions, each with bulk storage. It does not supply energy.
Advanced Output
The Advanced extended combined output port receives both product types. Its 6 item positions and 2 fluid positions are separate stores.
Reinforced In
The Reinforced extended combined input port has 12 item positions and 4 fluid positions.
Reinforced Out
The Reinforced extended combined output port has 12 item positions and 4 fluid positions.
Ultimate Input
The Ultimate extended combined input port has 18 item positions and 6 fluid positions, the largest layout in this family.
Ultimate Output
The Ultimate extended combined output port has 18 item positions and 6 fluid positions. It buffers multiple product types in one block.

All three tiers use bulk item and fluid storage. Right-click to inspect both resource groups, then configure their master and face switches separately on the $(l:mmcr:ports/auto_io)auto-IO page$(/l).$(br2)These ports provide neither energy nor chemical interfaces.
